clue.text: Rental mishaps spoilt ideal social system

indicators.note: something spoilt has been ruined and knocked out of its proper shape, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: both words taken as written, all thirteen letters used

explanation.surface: A landlord's run of bad luck with lettings wrecks somebody's utopian dream.
explanation.walkthrough: PHALANSTERISM is Fourier's scheme of people living in self-supporting communes called phalansteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Fourier proposed the phalanstery as a utopian commune, so his system was an idealised plan for organising society.

clue.text: Garden plants? Nasty disease enveloping odd ones in Hull

the last letter of the pox closes the wrapper

explanation.walkthrough: The disease POX opens round the odd letters of Hull: P(HL)OX. The question mark admits that the plant name works as a plural here.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a genus of garden flowers grown for their scented clusters, and the name serves for many plants.

clue.text: Your WI oddly appearing in dress as a caterpillar? (11, two words)

the rest of habit

explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's club. The jumbled letters go inside HABIT. The question mark warns that a woubit is a fuzzy caterpillar, so 'hairy' is part of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy woubit is an old dialect name for a woolly caterpillar, the hairy larva of a tiger moth.

clue.text: E.g. garter, as in elevated count

explanation.definitionFit: A leglet is an ornament worn round the leg, and a garter is one example of such a band.

clue.text: From Chesterfield perhaps, last achieving dominance? (4, two words)

explanation.walkthrough: Chesterfield looks like the town; it is the sofa. Moving its last letter to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As of introduces the date something starts, as in 'as of Monday', meaning from that time onward.

clue.text: Trooper abroad in due course joining conflict

clue.text: Two Canadian bucks? Front of hoof is round on one

the last letter of toe

clue.text: Many a series turning up includes this repeat

clue.text: Sweetened wine, once a source of inspiration when penning line

clue.text: Trim beard, fine one

clue.text: Sigh maybe as Special gets involved in rule over Ireland?

the rest of Eire

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts R above the rest: R + E(SP)IRE. 'Sigh maybe' is a definition by example.

clue.text: Language, one that's taught in school but not at work

explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests a classroom; it is a school of fish. This parse is the annotator's best reading of the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is an informal word for a language, especially a foreign one or a specialist jargon.

clue.text: 'Dark lady' for Shakespeare to court — disappointment follows

explanation.walkthrough: The Dark Lady of Shakespeare's sonnets is a red herring: the answer is his spelling of ouzel, the blackbird, so a dark lady is a female blackbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Woosel is Shakespeare's form of ouzel, the blackbird, as in 'the woosel cock so black of hue', a dark-feathered bird.

clue.text: Runner, once unpredictable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a skid or runner, as under a sledge
second meaning: an obsolete adjective for slippery and untrustworthy

explanation.surface: A former athlete was erratic in form.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipper is a skid on which something slides, and as an old adjective it meant slippery, hence not to be relied on.

clue.text: Paintings to preserve with containers

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
vases are containers for flowers

explanation.surface: Works of art are being stored away with some pots for safe keeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paintings are made on canvas, so a canvas is a common name for one picture.

clue.text: 'Tar-clad' etc, this could be cleanly extracted

definitions.text: 'Tar-clad' etc, this could be cleanly extracted

parts.note: the answer itself stands in for 'this'
taken as written
taken as written, the combined letters of the first two pieces

explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus the letters of TAR-CLAD ETC rearrange to CLEANLY EXTRACTED. The whole clue also describes the answer, which is distilled from coal tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylene is a hydrocarbon solvent obtained by distilling coal tar and wood tar, so it is literally extracted from tar.

clue.text: US novel, fifth print?

the rest of swelling

clue.text: Large stinger? Drunk another, first polished off

clue.text: E.g. pea stick stuck in meadow
